description: The tally filter system uses Vec<Box<dyn Filter>> + a Filter trait for runtime dispatch, which violates the workspace CLAUDE.md 'no trait objects — use enums for dispatch' rule. This is pre-existing (CellFilter/EnergyFilter/etc.) and was extended in op-6tz-notebooks-batch (SpatialLegendreFilter, MeshFilter). Refactor to a FilterKind enum so match sites are exhaustive and rust-analyzer navigable. Note: the moment-expansion path (SpatialLegendre depositing into all moment bins) needs a home in the enum design. Flagged in docs/ai-fleet-review/op-6tz-notebooks-batch/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md for human review.
title: outram-mc: refactor trait-object tally filter system (Vec<Box<dyn Filter>>) to enum dispatch

description: Discovered while building crates/outram-mc-tui (op-z5q/op-4h8): only physics::keff::run_keff (the bare-sphere-only driver) branches on KeffSettings::compute (ComputeType::CpuSingleThread/CpuMultiThread/Gpu). physics::transport_csg::run_keff_csg and pebble_beds::keff_delta::run_keff_delta both ignore the field entirely and always run the single-thread CPU path (verified: neither file references ComputeType/rayon/GpuContext at all). This means outram-mc-tui's compute-backend selector (CPU-single/CPU-multi/GPU) is currently inert for every one of its presets, since all four route through run_keff_csg or run_keff_delta, not run_keff. Follow-up: add the same ComputeType dispatch (rayon-parallel histories, GPU Sigma_t lookup with CPU fallback) to run_keff_csg and run_keff_delta that run_keff already has, so CSG and delta-tracking runs can actually use multi-core/GPU acceleration.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Landed + pushed (commit 0aee140 on claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9). run_keff_csg and run_keff_delta now dispatch on KeffSettings::compute: CpuSingleThread = existing deterministic reference; CpuMultiThread(ThreadCount) = new rayon-parallel per-generation history transport with per-history LCG jump-ahead seeding (thread-count-invariant, verified to the bit) via run_keff_csg_par / run_keff_delta_par; Gpu = honest fallback to CPU-multi (no GPU kernel for CSG/delta yet). run_keff_delta's closure gained a + Sync bound (all callers already satisfy it). V&V agreement tests added and passing: delta_multithread_agrees_with_single_thread (1.65 sigma) and csg_multithread_agrees_with_single_thread (0.47 sigma), both thread-count-invariant to the bit. TUI honesty notes + README corrected. The originally-reported gap (selector inert / drivers do not dispatch) is RESOLVED. Remaining GPU-kernel-for-CSG/delta work split out to op-9s8.

title: outram-mc-libs: run_keff_csg/run_keff_delta don't dispatch on ComputeType

description:
Found 2026-08-11 by the njoy/outram-mc agent while following the CLAUDE.md bookkeeping-pass routine, which tells agents to run `cargo fmt -p <crate>`.

MEASURED: `cargo fmt -p njoy-outram-park-fork -p outram-mc-libs` rewrote **222 files, +21 057 / -4 495 lines**. None of it was wanted; all of it was reverted and the real edits replayed by hand. The final semantic diff for that task was 4 files, +587/-48.

ROOT CAUSE: the repository is not rustfmt-clean and carries no `rustfmt.toml`, so `cargo fmt` reformats to upstream defaults across every file it touches, not just the ones being edited. The two conditions compound — no pinned style, and a large body of never-formatted legacy code.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE AGENT: the workspace CLAUDE.md "Bookkeeping pass" section instructs agents to run a formatter as part of a routine that is explicitly designed to be run per-crate by a fleet. Anyone who follows that instruction literally detonates a 20k-line diff into a branch, and if they do not notice, it lands. The instruction is currently a trap.

Also relevant: the same day, a `rustfmt --check` on four `tampines-steam-tables` files showed the legacy formatting problem directly — `ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs` would be substantially rewritten by rustfmt despite the change under review being three lines.

OPTIONS, maintainer's call:
1. Add a `rustfmt.toml` pinning the current style closely enough that a format pass is a no-op on untouched code, then format the workspace once in a single dedicated commit.
2. Format the workspace once, in its own commit, on a quiet branch, and accept the one-time churn — after which `cargo fmt -p` becomes safe and the CLAUDE.md instruction becomes true.
3. Amend CLAUDE.md to forbid `cargo fmt` and require `rustfmt` on individually named changed files only.

Until one of these is done, CLAUDE.md should carry a warning next to the bookkeeping-pass formatter step. Do NOT let an agent format the workspace as a side effect of unrelated work.
title: cargo fmt -p is destructive in this workspace: 222 files, +21057/-4495
